fixed.explanation: The dedicated worker session attach path never sends Emulation.setUserAgentOverride, so the worker keeps the default Accept-Language and navigator.languages. I added a call in the worker branch of _onAttachedToTarget. It sends the same override as _updateUserAgent when userAgent or locale is set. It uses _sendMayFail so a closed target doesn't break anything.

query.intent: When Chromium attaches to a new dedicated web worker session, the code sends user agent override (Emulation.setUserAgentOverride with userAgent and acceptLanguage) only for some cases. It must also send the override with the context locale to the dedicated worker's session, as is done for service workers.
query.symptom: Locale set on a browser context is not applied inside dedicated workers in Chromium: the worker's Accept-Language header and navigator.languages stay at the default English.
